correctness.rationale: For every state h, conditional survival integration yields mean stopped cost c_i(1-exp(-lambda_hi*t_i))/lambda_hi. Subtracting AB and BA factors precisely as (1-u_hA)(1-u_hB)(c_A/lambda_hA-c_B/lambda_hB), and mixing by the occupancy prior gives a single affine crossing iff signs oppose. A no-alarm prefix independently weights each state by S_h; Bayes posterior is the same interchange criterion times a strictly positive reach probability. All zero and boundary D_h cases follow from the exact affine identity. Independent rational substitutions reproduced D0=3/16, D1=-35/512, pi*=96/131, no-alarm posterior 9/13, and prefix interchange difference 69/40960; inspected checker_ordering.py tests direct stopped labor rather than assuming the formula. Domain: two prescribed positive-duration, positive-rate, positive-cost blocks, fixed latent state, immediate alarm stop and no sequence-dependent terminal charges. No general adaptive-policy optimality asserted.

value.rationale: The exact sharp prevalence threshold and an informative-block posterior reversal produce a reproducible qualitative scheduling boundary: the same two informative sensors reverse order solely after a negative alarm history, while consumed labor is measured continuously. This motivated two-state stochastic inspection specialization is useful for diagnosing why a fixed static sensor order can be suboptimal. It does not claim a new generic adjacent-interchange theorem.

limitations: Fixed independent state-conditional first-alarm Poisson hazards; fixed predetermined two-block order, no sensor-selection or adaptive multiblock optimality.
